canonical_statement: The study evaluated the efficacy and safety of the institution's standard intravenous UFH protocol in obese adults when dosing was based on adjusted body weight or total body weight.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a standard UFH protocol in obese patients using either ABW or TBW.

canonical_statement: This was a single-center retrospective observational cohort study at University of Florida Health Shands Hospital, a 1,162-bed academic medical center.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This was a single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study conducted at University of Florida Health Shands Hospital, a 1,162-bed academic medical center.

canonical_statement: Adjusted body weight was calculated as IBW + 0.4 × (TBW − IBW).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ABW was calculated using ideal body weight (IBW) as IBW + 0.4(TBW-IBW).

canonical_statement: The standard UFH protocol specified an 80 units/kg initial bolus, an 18 units/kg/h initial infusion, and an anti-Xa target of 0.3-0.7 units/mL, with titration based on repeat anti-Xa levels.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Initial bolus: 80 units/kg; Initial infusion rate: 18 units/kg/h; Goal anti-Xa level: 0.3-0.7 units/mL.

canonical_statement: The institutional protocol recommended adjusted body weight for intravenous UFH when patient weight exceeded 125 kg.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The UFH protocol recommends prescribers use ABW for patients weighing greater than 125 kg.

canonical_statement: The primary outcome was time from infusion start to the second of two consecutive therapeutic anti-Xa levels, with therapeutic anti-Xa defined as 0.3-0.7 units/mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary outcome was the time to two consecutive therapeutic UFH levels as measured by anti-Xa levels (goal 0.3 to 0.7 units/mL).

outcome.definition: Time from infusion start to the second consecutive anti-Xa level in the 0.3-0.7 units/mL range
